records.student_text: Sam walks toward the front of a train moving east at 9 m/s. Sam walks at 1 m/s relative to the train. Explain how Sam can be moving relative to the ground while also being described using a different motion relative to the train.
records.student_html:
Sam walks toward the front of a train moving east at 9 m/s. Sam walks at 1 m/s relative to the train. Explain how Sam can be moving relative to the ground while also being described using a different motion relative to the train.

  1. Sam is at rest relative to the ground because the train is the only valid frame.
  2. Reference frames change the object’s mass, which changes its motion.
  3. Relative to the train, Sam moves east at 1 m/s; relative to the ground, Sam moves east at 10 m/s. Motion depends on the chosen reference frame.
  4. Sam must have the same velocity in every reference frame.
choices: Sam is at rest relative to the ground because the train is the only valid frame.
Reference frames change the object’s mass, which changes its motion.
Relative to the train, Sam moves east at 1 m/s; relative to the ground, Sam moves east at 10 m/s. Motion depends on the chosen reference frame.
Sam must have the same velocity in every reference frame.
records.answer: Relative to the train, Sam moves east at 1 m/s; relative to the ground, Sam moves east at 10 m/s. Motion depends on the chosen reference frame.
records.solution_text: Use one reference frame at a time. The train-frame motion is the walking speed; the ground-frame motion combines the train motion and walking motion because both are east.
records.solution_html: Use one reference frame at a time. The train-frame motion is the walking speed; the ground-frame motion combines the train motion and walking motion because both are east.

records.student_text: On a elevator lobby, a rider’s speedometer reads 18 m/s at one instant. The rider’s average speed over the entire trip is 10 m/s. Explain what each value describes.
records.student_html:
On a elevator lobby, a rider’s speedometer reads 18 m/s at one instant. The rider’s average speed over the entire trip is 10 m/s. Explain what each value describes.

  1. The larger value is average and the smaller value is instantaneous by definition.
  2. 18 m/s is instantaneous speed at that moment; 10 m/s is total distance divided by total trip time.
  3. Both values are instantaneous because both use m/s.
  4. Both values are average because every speed is averaged over time.
choices: The larger value is average and the smaller value is instantaneous by definition.
18 m/s is instantaneous speed at that moment; 10 m/s is total distance divided by total trip time.
Both values are instantaneous because both use m/s.
Both values are average because every speed is averaged over time.
records.answer: 18 m/s is instantaneous speed at that moment; 10 m/s is total distance divided by total trip time.
records.solution_text: Instantaneous speed describes one moment. Average speed combines the whole interval: total distance divided by total elapsed time.
records.solution_html: Instantaneous speed describes one moment. Average speed combines the whole interval: total distance divided by total elapsed time.

A robot moves at a constant speed of 9 m/s. At first it moves east, then it turns and moves north while keeping the same speed. Compare its speed and velocity before and after the turn.

  1. Velocity has no direction, so only position changes.
  2. The speed remains 9 m/s, but the velocity changes because its direction changes from east to north.
  3. Both speed and velocity remain constant because the speedometer value is unchanged.
  4. The speed changes but the velocity does not.
choices: Velocity has no direction, so only position changes.
The speed remains 9 m/s, but the velocity changes because its direction changes from east to north.
Both speed and velocity remain constant because the speedometer value is unchanged.
The speed changes but the velocity does not.
records.answer: The speed remains 9 m/s, but the velocity changes because its direction changes from east to north.
records.solution_text: Velocity includes magnitude and direction. A direction change changes velocity even when the speed stays constant.
records.solution_html: Velocity includes magnitude and direction. A direction change changes velocity even when the speed stays constant.
